item.evidence: backend/projects.py:226 looks up only members.invite_token; :229-230 sets members.$.user_id to the caller without comparing members.email or marking the invite used. role_for at :33-35 grants the bound user that member's role. frontend/src/pages/AuthPages.jsx:72-75 automatically accepts the token.
item.expected: R-076: "is refused when the caller's email differs from the invited address" and "only once"; request: "An invite is sent to an email address." Acceptance must bind only that address and must not let another account replay it.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a signed-in recipient of a forwarded or leaked invite link can bind it to a different email, read the team's system and files, and, for an Editor invite, overwrite work. Reusing the link reassigns user_id again, potentially displacing the intended teammate. No owner approval is required; owner removal of the member is the available recovery.
reproduction_steps: As owner, invite teammate A as Editor and copy the invite link.
Sign in with a different email B and open that link.
The code accepts B and opens the project with Editor access.
Open the same link as another signed-in account; the membership is rebound again.
item.title: Anyone signed in with an invite link can take the invited teammate's access — acceptance never checks the invited email or consumes the token

item.evidence: backend/projects.py:163-168 reads and compares the version, then :169-172 find_one_and_update filters only project_id and increments version. frontend/src/pages/Workspace.jsx:273 sends base_version and :281 shows the warning only on 409.
item.expected: R-068: "you are warned before overwriting"; R-069: an older base_version "returns 409 ... and writes nothing"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "conditional/atomic operations" must protect concurrent commit points. Exactly one version-1 save may commit without a warning.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that two editors saving from version 1 concurrently can both pass the read-time check before either update. Both writes then succeed (versions 2 and 3), with the latter replacing the former system and inputs, and neither editor receives an overwrite warning. Consequential generated team work is lost without history (Phase 2 is not implemented).
reproduction_steps: Owner and Editor open the same version of a project.
Make different changes in each workspace.
Press Save in both while the requests overlap so both load the old version before either update.
Both return success; reopen and observe that only the later system remains, without a conflict dialog.
item.title: Two editors can silently overwrite each other's saves — version check is separate from the unconditional update

item.evidence: backend/auth.py:132 creates email accounts with email_verified False and :140-157 login never verifies them. backend/projects.py:34 grants an unclaimed email membership only if email_verified; :114-116 adds email matches to the shared query only for verified accounts.
item.expected: R-077 and request: "The person sees the project under 'Shared with me' as soon as they sign in with that email." Both supported sign-in methods must reach this outcome while maintaining secure email identity.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an invited email/password user signs in successfully but Shared with me stays empty, including when the owner invited an already registered email account. They must obtain and follow the separate invite link to gain access, defeating the promised automatic discovery. Google sign-in is the only path that sets verification (:170).
reproduction_steps: Create an email/password teammate account.
As owner add that email as Viewer or Editor in Share.
Sign in as that teammate without opening the invite link.
Open Shared with me: the query excludes the pending membership.
item.surface: Projects → Shared with me; email sign-in
item.title: Email/password invitees do not see invited projects on sign-in — automatic access is limited to Google-verified accounts

item.evidence: backend/projects.py:311-312 returns any file directly to its uploader for a viewer/read check, before :314 load_project. For reference files it also returns directly for editor/delete checks. :187-189 deleting a project only marks the project deleted and never marks files deleted. :341-349 loads references using this same bypass.
item.expected: Request: "Members can upload, download and delete files, according to their role"; R-065: deletion "removes the project and its files"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Follow ... membership removal ... through every supported access path." Project-linked files must always enforce the current project role and live-project state.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a removed Editor retains authenticated download access to every project file they uploaded even after membership removal or project deletion, and retains delete/use-in-generation access to their references after demotion to Viewer. This defeats the team's revocation boundary; the owner cannot revoke this file access through Share or project deletion.
reproduction_steps: As Editor upload a project file and attach a reference; retain their file ids.
As owner remove this Editor in Share (or delete the project).
As the former Editor request download of the uploaded file by its existing file id.
The uploader shortcut still serves it; a reference can also still be deleted or used in generation.
item.title: Removed teammates can still fetch their uploaded project files — uploader bypass skips current project permissions

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:189 stores project_context and notes in result.context; :154 initializes projectContext from browser storage; :288-298 restores dials/prompt/references but never calls setProjectContext(c.project_context); :301 unconditionally setNotes(""). :187 injects the current global projectContext into every run.
item.expected: R-062: reopening "restores those inputs and that system"; request: a project holds "description, dials, Project Context, modules and notes" and teammates regenerate together. Opening a cloud project must restore its own bias and notes rather than an unrelated browser default.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts opening project A saved with 'GAS with hard attribute ceiling' while the browser context is 'realistic large-scale FPS' leaves the FPS bias displayed and used in A's next regeneration. Notes that produced A are not restored to the notes control either. Saved context exists in Mongo but is ignored, so teammates and cross-device users must reconstruct it manually and can generate the wrong architecture.
reproduction_steps: Generate and save A with one Project Context preset and designer notes.
Change the browser's context to a different preset while working on B.
Open A from Projects.
A's saved context and notes are not restored; Synthesize sends the other preset.
item.surface: Projects → open; Project Context and Notes for next synthesis
item.title: Reopened projects use another project's bias and omit saved notes — openSystem never restores these inputs

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:156 maintains references separately; :189 copies them into result.context only when generation completes. :263-265 splitResult returns result.context unchanged; :270-274 saves that context. Files.jsx:43 and :61 update only the separate references state. openSystem at Workspace.jsx:298 restores context.references.
item.expected: R-078: "each attached reference ... stays attached to the project for later regenerations"; request: "Each can be removed individually." Saving must persist the currently chosen reference list without requiring another paid synthesis.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts an Editor attaching a file after synthesis then saving sees the chip disappear on reopening. Conversely removing a reference and saving restores the removed chip on reopening, and a later regeneration sends that reference again. Uploading the object with a project id does not fix the issue because project reopening never discovers attached references from the file collection. Regenerating before Save is a costly, undisclosed workaround.
reproduction_steps: Open a generated saved project.
Attach a new reference (or remove an existing reference chip).
Press Save without synthesizing again.
Reopen the project; the old reference list returns.
item.surface: Attach reference / remove chip → Save → reopen
item.title: Attaching or removing references on a saved project is lost on Save — persistence uses the last synthesis's stale reference list

item.evidence: App.js:27 routes every otherwise unmatched path to Workspace without extracting a project id. Workspace.jsx:168 only reads a ?project query; :171 immediately replaces even that URL with '/'. :305-311 opens project state without changing the URL.
item.expected: R-113: "Opening /projects/{id} directly ... loads that project's saved system ... and a reload keeps the same project open"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "direct access, reload, back and return paths" must retain the referenced object.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts opening /projects/<id> renders an unsaved default workspace, and reloading after opening a cloud project loses the selected project and inputs. Users must find it in Projects again; browser back/forward cannot return between project selections. Saved data remains recoverable through the list.
reproduction_steps: Open an existing project from Projects.
Reload the page: the workspace initializes with no project.
Open /projects/<that id> in a fresh signed-in tab.
The catch-all renders the default workspace without loading the id.
item.title: Reloading or deep-linking a cloud project opens the default workspace — project identity is never retained in the URL

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:187 awaits generation then :188-191 unconditionally replaces result using the original closure. :305-311 can independently replace project and result while the await runs. ProjectsPanel.jsx:90 open buttons remain enabled while busy (only Stack at :76 uses busy). Workspace.jsx:273 subsequently saves the displayed result to the currently selected project's id.
item.expected: Request: projects hold their own "latest generated system" and inputs; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "including late completion after cancel" and context restoration must preserve valid work.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a user generating A can open B during the 40–90 second job; A's delayed result then replaces B's displayed system while B's name, role and version stay selected. Pressing Save writes A's code and inputs over B without a conflict because B's version is current. There is no version history to recover B's overwritten system. The running task needs an operation/project identity guard or navigation protection.
reproduction_steps: Open A and start a regeneration.
Before it finishes, click B's Open row in Projects.
Wait for A's generation to finish; the header still names B but result/context come from A.
Press Save, then reopen B; its previous output has been replaced by A's generation.
item.title: Opening another project during synthesis can save the first project's output over it — late completion is not tied to its project

item.evidence: auth.py:127-134 permits registering an unverified email with a password. :168-171 merges a subsequent Google sign-in into that row and sets email_verified True, without removing or re-proving its existing password. :147-156 continues accepting that password. Project ownership is keyed by user_id (projects.py:31).
item.expected: R-055: "same email address ... one account" must preserve secure identity; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Establish the actual principals and trust model" and "OAuth ... link/create once". Linking a provider-verified email must not leave an unrelated unverified registrant with ongoing access.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts someone who pre-registers a teammate's email can keep their chosen password after the real teammate signs in with Google. The real teammate sees a successful Google session and creates private projects in the same user_id; the earlier registrant can log in by password to read or modify those projects and files. No victim password or Google credentials are required for the pre-registration. The victim would need owner-assisted reset to regain sole access.
reproduction_steps: Register an email/password account using another person's email (without email verification).
Have the actual email owner sign in through Google with that address and save a private project.
Sign in with the password chosen during pre-registration.
That session has the same user_id and can access the real owner's newly saved work.
item.surface: Email registration → Google account linking → email sign-in
item.title: A pre-registered password retains access to the real Google user's projects — account linking trusts an unverified existing email

item.evidence: auth.py:32 JWT payload has sub/type/exp but no session identity; :55-62 validates signature and user existence only. Logout :207-210 deletes only Google session rows and client cookies. Refresh :196-201 accepts the previous signed refresh token without a revoked-session lookup.
item.expected: Request: "sign-out"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "next-request rejection of revoked/deleted sessions" and "Sign-out ... ends a server-held session." A signed-out email session must not remain usable with its old credentials.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a retained email access token can continue reading and writing private projects for its remaining 15 minutes after Sign out; a retained refresh credential can mint further access for seven days. Clearing the UI cookies does not invalidate a captured session. Signing out therefore cannot terminate a compromised/shared email session; Google sessions do have a database deletion path.
reproduction_steps: Sign in with email/password and retain that session's credentials in an authorized API client.
Use Account menu → Sign out.
Reuse the old access credential for GET /api/projects; it remains accepted until expiry.
Reuse the old refresh credential for POST /api/auth/refresh; it can still renew access.
item.surface: Sign out; POST /api/auth/logout and /refresh; authenticated APIs
item.title: Signing out does not revoke email sessions — access and refresh JWTs have no server-side session or revocation check

item.evidence: Login.jsx:35-38 starts broker auth with redirect only, with no app nonce. App.js:21 accepts any session_id fragment. AuthPages.jsx:18-19 exchanges it immediately. auth.py:161-163 receives only session_id and verifies it with the provider but never binds it to a browser-initiated state.
item.expected: R-054: "checks the OAuth state value issued at sign-in start ... a callback whose state value does not match is refused"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "validate issued state." An uninitiated callback must not change the browser's signed-in identity.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an unsolicited callback URL containing a valid broker session identifier for a different account is exchanged and sets that account's session cookie, without proof that this browser initiated that login. A signed-out visitor can be logged into another person's account and unknowingly save private UE5 work there. Broker-side validity proves the identifier's identity, not this browser's intent; actual broker issuance behavior was not executed.
reproduction_steps: Obtain a valid broker callback identifier for account A in a controlled authentication flow.
In a different signed-out browser that never started Google login, open the app callback location carrying that identifier.
The frontend posts it and the backend sets account A's cookie without checking browser-bound state.
Saving work would then store it under A.
item.title: Unsolicited Google callbacks can log a visitor into another account — callback exchange lacks browser-bound state validation

item.evidence: changes.js:75-83 compactForApi sends only name/summary/modules/params/network notes and the first 2500 header characters; it drops cpp_source, pseudocode, graph and setup. Workspace.jsx:220 and :238 use it for regeneration and stacking. server.py:211-222 compacts again and :236 limits stacked headers to 1800 characters. :185-186 promises preserving unaffected content and integrating systems.
item.expected: R-087: previous output is sent with explicit revision instructions; request: "regeneration should visibly respect the edits" and stack should "combine them into a single synthesized output ... avoids conflicts." Unchanged implementation and cross-system logic must be available to the model for a faithful revision/merge.
item.observed: AI and model features: source proves custom behavior contained only in the previous .cpp, pseudocode, setup, graph or the omitted header tail is never sent on regeneration or stacking. For example, a saved damage system with a bespoke combo-reset rule only in its .cpp cannot have that rule preserved from the provided context when the user only changes Max Health, nor can stacking inspect its implementation conflicts. The model receives a summary, not the previous output. Output quality itself was not sampled; omitted context is deterministic and forces users to re-supply implementation manually.
reproduction_steps: Open a saved system whose .cpp contains an implementation detail not in its header or summary.
Change only a parameter and Synthesize, or select it with another project and Stack.
Trace compactForApi and build_user_text: the complete source, pseudocode and graph are absent from the model input.
The model cannot faithfully revise/merge that omitted implementation.
item.surface: Regenerate and Stack Systems model context
item.title: Regeneration and stacking cannot preserve existing implementation — both discard source, pseudocode, graph and most code before calling Claude

item.evidence: projects.py:22 sets TEXT_CHARS=20000; :261 takes PDF pages[:40] then text[:TEXT_CHARS]; :265 truncates decoded code/text to 20000 characters. :299-304 stores the full original size and reports successful attachment without a truncation flag. server.py:230-232 sends only that extracted text.
item.expected: R-104 and request: "AI uses them as source material", e.g. "extend this existing header"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Compare complete intended content and actual input selection" and make skipped input visible. Within the stated 10 MB acceptance limit, required content must reach the model or limitations must be communicated before synthesis.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts an accepted 30 KB .h whose class declaration lies after a long license/comment prefix loses that entire declaration before generation, and a PDF's page 41 is never considered. The chip still shows a successful attachment and the full file is stored, so developers pay for a synthesis that cannot follow the omitted specification without knowing to split/rewrite it. UTF-8 text and PDF extraction do reach Claude for content inside those silent bounds.
reproduction_steps: Attach a valid UTF-8 header under 10 MB with the declared class after character 20,000 (or a spec with requirements on PDF page 41).
Ask to extend that class or implement that requirement and Synthesize.
The model prompt receives only the truncated prefix.
No attachment or generation UI reports that the required content was omitted.
item.title: Accepted reference code and PDF content is silently omitted — extraction truncates at 20,000 characters and 40 pages

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:43-50 loops with a new setTimeout and GET every two seconds until five minutes, done or error; there is no AbortSignal or mounted guard. Workspace's only effect at :164-174 returns no synthesis cleanup. AuthContext.jsx:31-33 can unmount Workspace on sign-out. The polling catch at Workspace.jsx:48-49 also ignores permanent 401/404.
item.expected: R-118: polling "stops ... when ... user leaves the workspace"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "polling ends with its owner". Leaving a workspace must terminate its client polling and callbacks.
item.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source predicts signing out or navigating to a public share view during generation leaves the old polling loop alive for up to five minutes, issuing requests and (after sign-out) refresh attempts. Returning and starting another run adds a separate loop; old completions still issue progress/result callbacks and success toasts. The UI cannot cancel the abandoned loop. Normal completion does stop its loop.
reproduction_steps: Start Synthesize on a slow job.
Sign out or navigate within the app to another routed surface before it finishes.
Return to the workspace and start another generation.
The first loop has no cleanup and keeps polling alongside the new one until its deadline/completion.
item.title: Abandoned synthesis keeps polling after navigation or sign-out — async polling has no lifecycle cancellation

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:426 fixes left sidebar to w-[320px] shrink-0 and :606 fixes right sidebar to w-[340px] shrink-0 in a single flex row (:423), with main min-w-0 (:502). The header (:385-419) has unwrapped branding/actions. PublicView.jsx:35-51 also uses unwrapped full-text header/tab actions. index.css:57-59 and App.css:1 hide outer overflow; there is no responsive sidebar alternative.
item.expected: R-117: primary content and Synthesize/Copy JSON are usable "at 1440px and at 375px wide"; checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "containment ... scrolling and reachable controls under supported viewports." At narrow widths core output and actions must remain accessible.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts that at 375px the two fixed sidebars alone require 660px, exceeding the viewport by 285px before any center content. The right dials and generated output are clipped with no outer scrolling, and full-text public header/tab buttons overflow as well. A phone user cannot complete tuning/viewing/copying through the intended workspace. This is a source layout deduction, not a browser measurement.
reproduction_steps: Open the signed-in workspace at 375px CSS width.
Generate a system and try to view the central tabs and tune the right panel.
Open a public share link at the same width and try its Copy JSON and tab actions.
Fixed rows exceed the clipped viewport with no responsive navigation.
item.surface: Workspace and public share view at 375px width
item.title: Phone users cannot reach generated output and tuning actions — desktop-only fixed panels exceed a viewport with hidden overflow

item.evidence: index.css:21 defines --text-muted #64748b; :174 uses it for eyebrow text and :179 panels use #141923. Login.jsx:79 Forgot password and ProjectsPanel.jsx:94-96 saver metadata use text-muted. WCAG relative-luminance calculation from these exact hex colors gives (Llighter+.05)/(Ldarker+.05)=3.70:1 on #141923 and 3.94:1 on #0e121b, both below 4.5:1.
item.expected: R-115: "body text meets at least a 4.5:1 contrast against its background"; checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "contrast" must hold. The password-recovery control, metadata and small labels should be legible without relying on low-contrast text.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source-backed color calculation predicts low contrast for small recovery/help text and saved-by metadata across the new account/project surfaces. Users with reduced vision face extra reading difficulty, though the main content/actions remain available. Colors were calculated from source, not sampled from a rendered screenshot.
reproduction_steps: View Forgot password on the sign-in panel or saved-by metadata in Projects.
Resolve text-muted (#64748b) against the panel (#141923) or sidebar (#0e121b).
Compute WCAG contrast: 3.70:1 / 3.94:1 rather than the required 4.5:1.
item.surface: Sign-in help, Projects metadata, shared theme labels
item.title: Small recovery and saver text misses required contrast — muted text is only 3.70:1 against panels

item.evidence: Modal.jsx:5-9 only installs Escape; :11-12 renders aria-modal dialog/backdrop, but has no focus assignment, focus trap, background inertness or restore-focus logic. ShareModal.jsx:46 uses this primitive while Workspace's editing actions remain mounted; AccountMenu.jsx:19 uses it for admin reset.
item.expected: Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus stays visible and follows the active surface" and "Dialog close ... restores ... focus". Modal keyboard interaction must stay on the dialog rather than reaching covered workspace controls.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts keyboard users opening Share remain focused on the background Share button and can Tab through covered Copy, Export, Save, description and project controls before reaching modal fields. They can invoke covered actions while a supposedly modal share/reset/conflict surface is open. Closing does not restore focus. Pointer users can use the modal normally; keyboard users must traverse unrelated controls and risk acting on background work.
reproduction_steps: Focus the workspace Share button using the keyboard and press Enter.
Press Tab repeatedly.
Focus is not moved into or contained by the Share dialog, so background controls remain in the tab order.
Close the modal with Escape; no focus restoration is performed.
item.surface: Share, reset-link, migration and conflict modals
item.title: Keyboard focus escapes modal dialogs into covered workspace actions — modal primitive supplies no focus management

item.evidence: projects.py:281 preserves arbitrary original filenames; :330 removes only double quotes and :331 interpolates the name directly into the Content-Disposition header of starlette Response. requirements.txt pins starlette 0.37.2; header values use HTTP latin-1 encoding rather than Unicode filename* encoding. Files.jsx:19 needs that GET to succeed before creating a blob download.
item.expected: R-080/R-081: downloading returns "original name and identical bytes"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: preserve "encoding ... filename". A valid Unicode filename must not prevent delivery; use an encoded filename* with a safe fallback.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts uploading a valid file named '角色设计.txt' succeeds, but downloading it raises UnicodeEncodeError while constructing the response headers because those characters cannot be encoded as latin-1. A teammate/viewer receives a failed download instead of any bytes. An uploader could rename and re-upload outside the app, but recipients cannot fix the stored name themselves.
reproduction_steps: Upload a small project file named 角色设计.txt.
Open Files as a member and press Download.
The download endpoint attempts to place that raw name in its response header and fails before delivering the file.
item.title: Files with non-Latin filenames cannot be downloaded — raw Unicode is placed into a latin-1 HTTP header

item.evidence: CompareView.jsx:34 passes params:{} and notes:"" to computeChanges and :35 removes every module change. Workspace.jsx:248-254 mutates result.modules before regeneration; :188 sets that already-edited result as previousResult. computeChanges (changes.js:27-40) only detects params/notes when supplied and needs original module state.
item.expected: R-094: Compare "lists which inputs changed" across "parameters and modules"; request: "see the effect of dial or prompt changes"; R-086 includes parameter values, module toggles/additions and notes. Compare's previous side and changed-input list must reflect the actual previous synthesis, not edited chips.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a regeneration changing Max Health, toggling StaminaDrain and adding notes opens Compare with no corresponding Input changes chips. Its Parameters & Modules view also uses the already-toggled old module state, so a module removal can show no before/after module difference. Code/text line diff still works, but users cannot reliably audit which requested edits produced it.
reproduction_steps: Generate a system with a parameter and an enabled module.
Change that parameter, toggle the module off, add notes and Synthesize.
Inspect Compare's Input changes: those edits are omitted.
Switch to Parameters & Modules: the previous module is already off, hiding the actual toggle.
item.surface: Compare → Input changes and Parameters & Modules
item.title: Compare hides parameter/module/note edits and misstates old module selection — it discards those input changes and snapshots edited state

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:152 previousResult is only React state; :188 assigns it after an in-session run. splitResult :263-265 exports/saves result only, with no previousResult. openSystem :300 explicitly clears previousResult. backend/projects.py:127-132 stores only current system/context; :169-172 replaces them on save. CompareView.jsx:44-49 then shows 'Synthesize twice'.
item.expected: R-095's independently checkable outcome is retrieval of previous/current sections for a cloud project; request: "Stack Systems and Compare keep working with cloud projects" and Phase 2 adds "any earlier version, not just the last one." Phase 1 should retain the immediate before/after comparison across save and reopen, without requiring full Phase 2 history or a particular API route.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts a developer synthesizing twice, comparing and saving a cloud project loses the previous side after reload/reopen. Another Editor opening that saved project cannot inspect the changes at all. They must pay for another regeneration just to create a new pair, and the original comparison cannot be reconstructed through the app because the previous output was discarded.
reproduction_steps: Generate, tune and regenerate a system, then inspect Compare.
Save the project and reopen it (or open it on another device).
Open Compare: only the empty 'Synthesize twice' message is available.
No saved previous synthesis or changed-input record can be loaded.
item.title: Cloud projects lose their before/after comparison on reopening — only the current synthesis is persisted

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:330-334 posts every migration item to /projects/import and the Import them button at :752 has no busy guard. projects.py:152 calls create each time; :128 mints a new project_id and :133 inserts without a legacy-source identity check. server.py:42-49 has no owner/legacy-id uniqueness index.
item.expected: R-085: posting the same browser library twice "creates no duplicate project"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Establish logical record/operation/effect identity ... retries ... concurrent creation." A given browser-saved system imported by one migration intent must create one cloud copy, while distinct legacy systems remain distinct.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts clicking Import them twice while migration is in progress or retrying its request duplicates each legacy system under fresh ids. The modal remains actionable throughout and the backend has no idempotency key. The user's cloud library becomes cluttered with duplicate projects; manual deletion is the safe recovery.
reproduction_steps: Have multiple systems in the old browser library and sign in for the first time.
Click Import them twice before the first network loop finishes (or retry the same import payload).
Both loops POST the same entries.
Mine contains separately identified duplicates of each imported system.
item.title: Retrying browser migration duplicates saved systems — every import mints a fresh project with no legacy identity

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:334 swallows every failed per-item import; :336 emits a success toast even for zero imported; :339 writes the migration-completed key regardless of failures and :340 closes the modal. Initialization at :166-167 offers migration only if that key is absent. Browser data is not removed, but no retry UI exists.
item.expected: R-084: "Import creates one project per browser system"; request: "Import them copies them into the account"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "Walk failure boundaries for batches ... visible rejected/skipped input". Partial failures must be explained and retryable rather than marking unfinished migration complete.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a transient network/storage failure during first migration leaves some or all systems unimported, then permanently suppresses the offer and labels the operation with a success toast. The raw legacy data remains in localStorage, but the new cloud-only library has no control to reopen or retry that browser library, so the user cannot recover through the intended UI without developer/storage intervention.
reproduction_steps: Start first-sign-in Import them with legacy systems present.
Have one or more POST /projects/import requests fail (e.g. a transient network interruption).
After the loop the modal closes and reports Imported N of M.
Reload: the completion marker prevents another migration offer despite the missing projects.
item.title: Failed browser migrations cannot be retried in the app — failures are swallowed and the one-time prompt is marked complete

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:418 Save is disabled only when !result or readOnly, not while saving. :272-274 uses captured project state; before the first POST resolves, a second call still sees project null and POSTs again. projects.py:128/133 always mints and inserts another project, with no create operation identity.
item.expected: Checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "pending controls and server-side operation identity preserve one create ... per intent"; request: "Save ... work as they do today, but in the cloud." Repeated clicks during a single initial Save should create one project.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a developer double-clicking Save project on an unsaved synthesis gets two distinct cloud projects. The UI provides no pending state and both calls show success. Manual deletion is a safe but unnecessary cleanup; this is separate from migration duplication because normal saves use a different entry point and have no migration source id.
reproduction_steps: Generate an unsaved system.
Click Save project twice before the first request returns.
Both captured calls choose POST /projects.
Projects → Mine contains two copies of the same initial save.
item.title: Double-clicking Save project creates duplicate cloud projects — initial save has no pending guard or operation identity

item.evidence: projects.py:125 checks only truthy system_name; :147 accepts the whole imported dict as a system and :151-152 stores it without SystemOutput validation. Workspace.jsx:299 renders it, :362 calls tunable_parameters.forEach and :659 calls modules.map. No error boundary is present in App.js:32-40.
item.expected: Checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: "malformed/partial input ... visible rejected/skipped input"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "fields, types" must match at both ends; R-082/R-083 promise usable project import. Malformed project JSON must be refused without storing a broken project or crashing the workspace.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: source predicts importing valid JSON with a system_name but tunable_parameters set to a string (or non-array modules) stores the record and then causes an uncaught frontend TypeError when ProjectsPanel opens it. The workspace becomes unusable rather than explaining the invalid file. Reload resets the open project, allowing the user to delete the broken row; ordinary valid exports do round-trip system/context correctly.
reproduction_steps: Use Import project with a JSON object containing system_name 'Broken' and tunable_parameters 'bad'.
The server accepts it because system_name is truthy.
The import UI immediately opens it.
Workspace's forEach/map assumptions throw instead of showing an import-validation message.
item.title: Malformed imported project JSON crashes the workspace after being saved — importer validates only system_name

item.evidence: server.py:128 makes setup why optional with default ''; :150 defaults applied_changes to []; :143-148 accepts empty code strings and empty graph/setup lists. :303 performs only SystemOutput(**data), then :308 marks done. There is no comparison against req.change_requests, req.parameter_overrides or required output completeness. ChangePanels.jsx:36-38 hides the panel entirely when changes are absent.
item.expected: R-087: "one applied entry per queued change"; R-089: why notes explain setup decisions; R-097: non-empty complete code/graph/setup; R-102: requested values are used. Checklist, AI and model features: "parsing, semantic validation ... empty/malformed results ... to the user-visible outcome." A structurally valid but incomplete/unapplied reply must not be confirmed as completed synthesis.
item.observed: AI and model features: source proves that if Claude returns a JSON object with all required keys but empty code, empty graph/setup lists, no applied_changes, or a tunable value different from an explicit override, the backend records done and the UI announces success. A user requesting Max Health=250 can receive and save a 100-valued output, with no row explaining that edit; empty output is also accepted. This is a conditional source trace of an accepted bad provider reply, not an observed model failure. Users must manually audit/retry paid generations instead of trusting the promised feedback.
reproduction_steps: Queue a parameter change and a designer note, then Synthesize.
Consider a provider reply with the expected field types but applied_changes omitted and tunable value unchanged (or empty code/graph lists).
SystemOutput validation accepts it and marks the job done.
The UI shows success and hides the missing change report rather than rejecting/reconciling the incomplete result.
item.surface: Claude response → completed synthesis and Applied in this synthesis
item.title: Incomplete or unhonored generations are reported as successful — output validation checks types but not required content or edit coverage

item.evidence: auth.py:229 reads a reset record; :230 checks used; :232 changes the password; only afterward :233 sets used=True using a token-only filter. There is no atomic used=False claim or transaction before the password write. ResetPassword in AuthPages.jsx:42-58 has no busy guard against overlapping submissions.
item.expected: R-059: the reset token is "single-use" and "a second use ... is refused"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "conditional/atomic operations" must preserve effect identity under concurrent requests. Only one password change may succeed for a given token.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts two concurrent requests with the same reset link and different new passwords can both observe used=False and both report success, with the second password winning. The first user is then unable to sign in with the password the screen confirmed. A person retaining the same reset URL can race a legitimate redemption; another admin reset link is needed to recover safely.
reproduction_steps: Obtain a fresh on-screen reset link.
Submit that token concurrently from two clients with different valid new passwords, before either marks it used.
Both requests can pass the unused check and update the password.
Only the last password works despite both submissions reporting success.
item.title: One reset link can change the password twice concurrently — token consumption happens after an unguarded password write

item.evidence: auth.py:174-178 creates Google-first users without password_hash. :128-129 rejects every registration for an existing email; :148 rejects email sign-in when password_hash is missing. No set-password/account-link action exists in AccountMenu.jsx:58-65; only an admin can issue a reset link (:214-224).
item.expected: R-055: "Signing in with Google ... and later registering with email/password ... reaches one account"; request: "Two ways to sign in ... If both use the same email address, they reach the same account." Provide a secure authenticated way to add the password method to the existing account, without creating a duplicate.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a Google-first user trying Create account with the same email is refused, and Sign in with email always fails because no password exists. They can continue using Google, but cannot add the promised second method without owner-assisted password reset, which is not an ordinary self-service linking flow.
reproduction_steps: Sign in for the first time using Google and save a project.
Sign out and choose Create account with the same email and a password.
Registration says the account already exists.
Try email Sign in: the Google-first record has no password, and there is no account control to set one.
item.title: Google-first users cannot add email/password sign-in themselves — registration rejects their email and no password-linking flow exists

item.evidence: projects.py:113/:117 use to_list(500) with no skip/cursor/total; :322 also caps file listing at 500. ProjectsPanel.jsx:71 labels lists[id].length as the count and :86 renders only those rows, with no paging/Load more action. ProjectFiles similarly renders the returned files only (:119).
item.expected: Request: cloud Projects "saved safely and available on any device" and Files keeps project artifacts; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation" and "counts ... match the rows they summarize." All stored accessible projects/files must remain discoverable as the library grows.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that once a user has 501 live owned projects (including repeated imports) their oldest project disappears from Mine and the count reads 500, with no way to load the remaining page. Likewise a project's 501st-oldest file is omitted from Files. Records are still stored and retrievable if an id was retained, but ordinary users cannot discover/download older work through the UI on a new device.
reproduction_steps: Accumulate or import 501 distinct projects in one account.
Open Projects → Mine; only the newest 500 appear with count 500.
Look for the oldest project or a next-page control: neither is available.
The same cutoff applies after uploading more than 500 project files.
item.surface: Projects lists and Files tab at more than 500 records
item.title: Older projects and files silently disappear from their lists — fixed 500-record caps have no pagination or truncation notice

item.evidence: projects.py:261 uses only PdfReader page.extract_text() for PDF references. upload_file :294-295 calls it for any non-image reference; load_references :347-349 attaches image_bytes only when content_type starts image/. server.py:230 sends extracted PDF text, while :285 includes only image_bytes as visual content.
item.expected: Request: "Accepted types are screenshots and images, PDFs" and "The AI uses them as source material"; R-104; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: trace "complete intended content and actual input selection". A valid PDF whose content is graphical must reach the model visually or be explicitly rejected/warned, not silently treated as empty source.
item.observed: AI and model features: source predicts a scanned spec or PDF containing a UI screenshot but no text layer uploads successfully yet supplies an empty body to Claude. No PDF bytes or rendered page images reach the model and no empty-extraction warning appears. The designer's request to match that PDF cannot be grounded in its actual content; converting it manually to an image is a safe workaround once the limitation is discovered.
reproduction_steps: Attach a valid image-only PDF under 10 MB containing the desired UI/spec.
Ask Synthesize to follow it.
extract_text returns empty text and no image_bytes are generated for application/pdf.
The model request contains the filename but none of the PDF's visible source content.
item.title: Image-only PDFs are accepted but invisible to Claude — PDF processing extracts text only and sends no visual pages

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:187 awaits the long-running job; :189 snapshots the notes submitted at start; :190 unconditionally clears the live notes state on completion. The notes textarea at :702-710 is inside a fieldset disabled only by readOnly (:608), not loading, so users can keep editing notes while the job runs.
item.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: input and operation state must remain coherent. R-086/request: notes before the next Synthesize must be injected rather than silently discarded.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a developer entering new notes for the next pass while Claude is generating loses those notes when the old request completes. They were not in that request's body, are not in result.context, and are erased from the visible field with no warning. Rewriting the short draft is the only recovery; controls suggest editing remains allowed during generation.
reproduction_steps: Start a synthesis or regeneration.
While it is running, type a new note such as 'use a Gameplay Tag for stun' in Notes for next synthesis.
Wait for the current job to complete.
The new note disappears although it was never sent to that job or saved in its context.
item.surface: Notes for next synthesis during a running generation
item.title: Notes typed while a synthesis is running disappear on completion — the old request unconditionally clears the live draft

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:36-38 keeps job_id only in a local async variable; no component/localStorage/project field stores it and mount at :164-174 loads only templates/migration/query project. server.py:315-318 persists jobs but only :325-330 GET-by-id retrieves them; there is no current/recent job lookup or result recovery consumer.
item.expected: Checklist, Business logic and calculations: "interruption ... revisit ... resume ... retrieves the completed session" where supported; users rely on: "A paid background synthesis can be retrieved after an ordinary page reload rather than requiring a second paid run." R-099/R-100 describe server background generation and delivery of its finished system.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts reloading during a generation loses the job id and returns to an idle workspace even though the server keeps generating and spending the owner's credits. The completed result remains in Mongo but is unreachable through any workspace/library action; only someone who retained the API id can retrieve it. The ordinary UI recovery is to pay for another synthesis. Normal uninterrupted polling delivers the result.
reproduction_steps: Press Synthesize and wait until the background job has started.
Reload the browser before it finishes.
The new workspace starts idle with no resume/recent-job control.
Allow the original job to finish: it is not shown or recoverable in Projects unless the original page had saved its result.
item.title: Reloading strands the paid synthesis result — the only job handle exists inside the old polling call

item.evidence: projects.py:284 executes data = await file.read() without a size bound, then :285-287 applies 10/25 MB limits using len(data). The multipart UploadFile may be disk-spooled, but this call materializes the entire uploaded body in application memory before rejection.
item.expected: Request: "10 MB per reference file and 25 MB per project file"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "buffering ... bounds and backpressure" must prevent material resource growth for reachable input. Oversized uploads must be rejected without unbounded application-memory buffering.
item.observed: Performance and resource leaks: source predicts a signed-in user's oversized 1 GB upload is fully read into a bytes object before its eventual 413, and concurrent such uploads multiply the allocation. The documented 25 MB ceiling therefore does not bound worker memory, risking interruptions to other users' saves/generations under a reachable large-upload workload. No runtime memory/latency measurement was made; exact failure depends on deployment memory.
reproduction_steps: As a member with Editor access, upload a project file much larger than 25 MB.
The endpoint reads the full file into memory first.
Only after that allocation does it return the size-limit error.
Concurrent oversized uploads repeat that full allocation per request.
item.title: Oversized uploads can exhaust worker memory before rejection — file limits are checked only after an unbounded read

item.evidence: api.js:11 excludes every URL beginning /auth/ from refresh/retry. AccountMenu.jsx:14 posts /auth/admin/reset-link, whose backend Depends(admin_user) calls current_user and returns 401 after the 15-minute access expiry (auth.py:16,86-96). The refresh cookie remains valid seven days (:17,42).
item.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "Trace token storage ... expiry ... refresh/retry where refresh tokens exist"; R-058: admin can create an on-screen reset link. An active admin with a valid refresh session must not need unrelated navigation or reload for this protected account action.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts an email-signed-in admin waiting over 15 minutes then choosing Password reset link receives 'Not authenticated' on Create, repeatedly, despite the still-valid refresh session. Other project API calls refresh automatically, but this action never does. Reloading or forcing an unrelated project request restores it; this is bounded but confusing account-management failure.
reproduction_steps: Sign in as admin using email/password.
Wait beyond the 15-minute access-token lifetime without making a refreshing API call.
Open Account menu → Password reset link and press Create for a valid user.
The /auth/ exclusion prevents refresh, so Create fails until reload or another non-auth API call renews access.
item.surface: Account menu → Password reset link → Create
item.title: Admin reset-link creation stops working after access-token expiry — refresh interceptor skips protected auth routes

item.evidence: server.py:77 configures extra='ignore'; GenerateRequest :79-95 has no project_id and generate_system :312 requires only current_user, not load_project(..., 'editor'). Workspace.jsx:213-221 sends a previous system without project identity; only the frontend readOnly flag at :161 and fieldsets prevent Viewer synthesis. In contrast projects.py:163 and :279-280 do check editor access for saves/uploads.
item.expected: R-073: "a generate request attributed to that project [from a Viewer is] refused ... while ... Editor ... succeed"; request: "Viewer: can open, copy, export and download only"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: reject "client-only checks without server enforcement." Project regeneration must enforce the current project's role server-side.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts a Viewer sending a project regeneration directly can start a paid Claude job and obtain its revised output because project identity is ignored, whereas the UI says regeneration requires Editor access. Saving back to the shared project is correctly refused, so this is a bounded generation-role violation rather than unauthorized durable project mutation. The endpoint must distinguish an allowed new personal synthesis from a regeneration of an existing role-restricted project.
reproduction_steps: Open a project shared as Viewer and note that Synthesize is disabled.
Using an authorized API client, submit its regeneration request with that project's identity and previous output.
GenerateRequest ignores the project identity and starts a job for the Viewer.
The same request is never checked against the member's current Viewer role.
item.title: Viewer project regeneration is restricted only in the UI — generation requests have no enforced project identity or Editor check

item.evidence: server.py:94 declares stack_systems max_length=4 with no minimum for a nonempty list. :235-237 treats any nonempty list as stacking, and :312-319 starts a job without validating at least two systems. ProjectsPanel.jsx:76 correctly disables Stack for fewer than two, so only the client enforces this boundary.
item.expected: R-093: "fewer than 2 or more than 4 ... refused and starts no generation"; request: "select two or more saved systems and combine them." A stack request with one source must be rejected before spending generation credits (empty stack_systems must remain valid for ordinary non-stack synthesis).
item.observed: Business logic and calculations: source predicts a caller submitting one system in stack_systems receives a paid background stack job rather than a validation error. It cannot combine two systems and returns stacked_from naming just one. The regular UI avoids this request, and the upper four-source boundary is enforced; this is a bounded backend contract/input-validation failure.
reproduction_steps: Submit POST /api/generate with a valid prompt and stack_systems containing one saved system.
The request passes Pydantic validation.
A background generation starts and is instructed to merge a single system instead of refusing the invalid stack.
item.title: Single-system stack requests spend credits instead of being rejected — backend stack validation has no lower bound

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:398-399 makes the project name a button; :318 calls window.prompt('Project name', project.name). There is no inline input/edit mode. PATCH persists the accepted name at :321 and backend/projects.py:178-182.
item.expected: R-064 and request: "The top bar gains the project name (editable in place)." Renaming should edit the displayed top-bar name in the workspace rather than opening a separate native prompt.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts clicking the name opens the browser's blocking prompt instead of an in-place field. Rename persistence and cancel safety work, so this is minor interaction/design friction, not lost data or inability to rename.
reproduction_steps: Open an owned or editable project.
Click the project name in the top bar.
A native window.prompt opens rather than making that name editable in place.
item.title: Project names are not editable in place — rename opens a native blocking prompt

item.evidence: auth.py:102/:113 accepts passwords up to 128 characters, :24 hashes password.encode() directly and :28 verifies the same way. backend/requirements.txt pins bcrypt==4.1.3, whose bcrypt input semantics use only the first 72 bytes. There is no byte-length validator or full-length prehash.
item.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "password hashing" and valid/wrong-password handling must preserve the supported password's identity; users rely on: "All characters of an accepted password determine whether it authenticates." For a reset, changing a supported password must invalidate the old distinct password, not ignore its suffix.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts two accepted passwords sharing the first 72 UTF-8 bytes but differing later authenticate as the same password. A user resetting an 80-character passphrase by changing its tail can still sign in with the old password, and Unicode passwords reach this byte boundary with fewer than 72 characters. The remaining prefix still supplies entropy, so the evidence supports a bounded password-identity failure rather than a general bypass. Users are not told to change the earlier prefix to recover.
reproduction_steps: Register using a valid password longer than 72 UTF-8 bytes but within the 128-character limit.
Through a fresh reset link choose a different password with the same first 72 bytes and a changed suffix.
Sign out and try the old password.
bcrypt 4.1.3 ignores the differing suffix and accepts the old password too.
item.surface: Email registration, sign-in and password reset with long/Unicode passwords
item.title: Accepted long passwords ignore their suffix, so an old password can survive reset — bcrypt's 72-byte limit conflicts with the 128-character input contract

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:38-40 treats a failed POST response as a failed generation without reconciling a possible job already started. server.py:314-319 creates a fresh random job id and task on every POST, with no caller-supplied operation key/unique intent lookup. The client retains no pending operation handle before the POST response.
item.expected: Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "retries ... preserve the operation's identity" and "a send timing out after delivery must reconcile before retrying"; request: "Every AI generation ... is paid from the app owner's ... balance." One synthesis intent must not incur two generations solely because its accepted response was lost.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts that if the server creates a job but its initial POST response is lost, the UI immediately reports failure and allows Retry/Synthesize. Retrying creates a second independent Claude call while the first continues spending credits; the first result is unreachable through the UI. Any signed-in developer on an unreliable connection can unintentionally charge the owner twice for one requested synthesis. The issue is retry identity, distinct from duplicate cloud Save records.
reproduction_steps: Start Synthesize.
Have the initial POST response fail after the backend has inserted the job and started its task.
After the visible Generation failed message, press Synthesize again.
The backend starts a second job rather than returning/recovering the first operation.
item.surface: Synthesize → ambiguous initial network failure → retry
item.title: Retrying a lost synthesis response spends credits twice — generation creation has no stable operation identity

item.evidence: NodeGraph.jsx:29-31 computes graph bounds then clamps the fit zoom to at least 0.3. :33 aligns its minimum corner rather than adding any alternate overview. :51-53 permits dragging nodes arbitrarily far apart. Thus a graph whose width is 5000 units requires at least 1500px at minimum zoom, even if the canvas is only 780px wide.
item.expected: R-109: "Fit button frames every node in view"; checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: containment under supported content variation. Fit must choose a zoom that accommodates the current dragged graph bounds, not stop above that required scale.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts after panning/dragging a node far from the rest, Fit still clips distant nodes because its 30% floor prevents scaling them into the canvas. Users can recover by panning or Reset (which discards manual positioning), so this is minor graph-navigation friction, not lost generated code. The numeric witness is a source geometry calculation, not a measured viewport render.
reproduction_steps: On a roughly 780px-wide event canvas, repeatedly pan and drag a node until the graph spans about 5000 coordinate units.
Press Fit.
The fit calculation bottoms out at 0.3, so the graph still occupies at least 1500px and cannot show all nodes.
Use pan or Reset to recover visibility.
item.title: Fit can leave dragged nodes offscreen — its minimum zoom prevents framing a widely spread graph
